title: Expansion manual approval binding
description: Objective: bind one scheduler-admitted expansion and its stored prepared funding/resource/fence identity to one exact manual graph approval, with every changed byte requiring reapproval. Hard dependencies: task-2561a780fdd149439c9858c9c7b459e8 and Graph supersession engine task-dddfaf83f9c644099b5b263e485c58c7 must be DONE. Deliverable: focused core preparation and approval reducers that compose the landed policy/approval/graph/supersession decisions without minting child execution authority. NOT in scope: automatic approval, daemon persistence/transactions, scheduler validation, child activation, supersession execution, or UI. Owned paths: packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-preparation.ts, expansion-preparation.js, expansion-approval.ts, expansion-approval.js, expansion-approval.test.ts. Production consumer: task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2. Verification: pnpm --filter @moe/core typecheck && pnpm --filter @moe/core test.
definitionOfDone: Preparation validates and freezes the complete admitted proposal/revision, quality/dependency, scope/oracle/input, budget reservation, resource reservation, fairness opportunity/cap revision, supersession disposition/funding/fence, policy, goal version, graph epoch, source facts, and deadline into one canonical identity.

Manual approval composes the existing policy, ApprovalDecisionRecord, graph revision, and supersession decisions and succeeds only when every approval hash/ref/criteria/scope/budget/resource/quality/dependency/policy/preparation byte matches the current stored identity.

Any missing, UNKNOWN, expired, released, invalidated, consumed, stale, mismatched, or concurrently changed fact refuses with exact stable code and layer, preserves the prepared/graph/approval inputs unchanged, and returns no child run/lease/effect/slot/allocation activation/dispatch authority.

Focused tests perturb every bound field, race approve with release/invalidate/expiry/reprepare, assert duplicate byte-identical replay, manual-only eligibility, exact code plus layer and refusing component, nonzero generated cases, zero partial authority, and production mutations turning red.
The exact verification command exits 0, production files remain below 400 lines, automatic approval is absent, and task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2 is recorded as the durable consumer.
taskRails: Policy ALLOW can make the proposal eligible for review but cannot approve it in this task.
Do not duplicate supersession/funding/fence authority; consume its exact landed production records.
Actual atomic durable activation and child authority remain owned by daemon composition.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED for preparation (DoD 1). Create packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-approval.test.ts covering the preparation half first.

DoD 1 lists thirteen fact families that must be validated and FROZEN into ONE canonical identity: admitted proposal/revision, quality/dependency, scope/oracle/input, budget reservation, resource reservation, fairness opportunity/cap revision, supersession disposition/funding/fence, policy, goal version, graph epoch, source facts, and deadline. Assert each is bound, and — the load-bearing property — that PERTURBING ANY ONE OF THEM YIELDS A DIFFERENT IDENTITY. Test that field by field, not with a single happy-path digest; DoD 4 says "perturb every bound field".

A digest asserted only for presence rots silently while the value changes every run. Assert exact equality for the stable case and exact INEQUALITY for each perturbation.

Since the admitted facts arrive as data, malformed or partial inbound records are a first-class case: a record missing a family, carrying an extra key, or carrying an UNKNOWN value must refuse with an exact code and layer — never be normalised or defaulted.

Use a real temp-free pure test; this is a pure kernel with no store. Assert the generated sweep produced a NON-ZERO case count.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed for the preparation half. Created packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-approval.test.ts (pure, no temp files, no store).

RED evidence, run fresh: `pnpm exec vitest run --root . packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-approval.test.ts` -> exit 1, "Error: Cannot find module './expansion-preparation.js'". Fails because the production module is absent, not from a typo.

WHAT THE SUITE PINS.
- Closed vocabulary asserted by exact value, not membership: 9 codes, 9 layers (BUDGET, EVIDENCE, FENCE, FUNDING, INPUT, LIFECYCLE, POLICY, RESOURCE, SUPERSESSION_KERNEL), 4 components (EXPANSION_PREPARATION, GRAPH_REVISION, POLICY_EVALUATION, SUPERSESSION_ENGINE).
- 30 single-field identity perturbations via it.each, each asserting exact INEQUALITY against the baseline identity, plus exact equality for the stable case and for byte-identical replay.
- Sweep is policed against a HAND-WRITTEN name list and an exact count of 30, and against a hand-written 17-entry family set, so a shrunken generator cannot pass by emitting fewer cases (mem:qa-generated-table-cannot-police-its-own-generator).
- Refusals asserted as the full object {code, component, layer, ok} — every one names its layer AND its refusing component, never merely "it refused".
- Delegated supersession refusals assert the kernel's own REVISION_REBOUND / SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED with layer SUPERSESSION_KERNEL verbatim, so a local synonym would redden.
- Missing family, extra key, UNKNOWN truth class, released budget, released resource, consumed funding, unfenced authority, non-supersedable graph lifecycle, malformed policy input, DENY and HOLD_UNKNOWN outcomes each get their own exact-code test.
- Deep-freeze assertion walks the whole result recursively (a shallow freeze passes Object.isFrozen on the root, so the recursive walk is the only thing that can catch it).
- Zero-authority assertion collects every key in the result recursively, asserts the collected key count is NON-ZERO first (so an empty walk cannot pass vacuously), then asserts nothing matches /run|lease|effect|slot|allocation|dispatch|activat/iu.
- Inputs-unchanged assertion compares before/after JSON serialisations of the input, not the return value.

DESIGN LOCKED BY THE TESTS, and it is the anti-duplication ruling from step 1 made concrete: bound has exactly 8 top-level keys — admitted, criteria, deadlineEpochMs, fence, funding, graphLifecycle, policyDecision, supersessionAuthorityHash. The graph binding scalars (revisionId, graphContentHash, graphEpoch) are NOT bound beside supersessionAuthorityHash; they are bound ONCE, inside the kernel-computed authorityHash, and reached through sources.supersession.expectedPredecessor whose integrity the recomputed hash proves. Same for the policy evaluation input. That is why the graph-epoch and graph-content-hash perturbations edit the supersession pair rather than a separate field: had both been bound, dropping either from the identity would have left its perturbation test green — the exact defect mem:gotcha-a-digest-can-mask-every-field-it-covers records from the producer task.

Policy fixture uses an R2 DAEMON_VERIFIED fact so evaluatePolicy yields REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL through the landed design-710 human-only-tier path; DENY and HOLD_UNKNOWN are reached by flipping a rule effect and by emptying facts, so all three outcomes come from the production evaluator rather than from hand-written records.

MEASURED: expansion-preparation.ts = 358 physical lines by `grep -c ''` (under the 400 cap; above the 250 target, disclosed rather than hidden — the file is one closed-shape validator per fact family plus the identity derivation, and the only split available would put a third production module outside this task's five owned paths).

WHAT IT DOES. Closed shape check on the whole envelope (`exact` + `snapshotData` from the landed policy boundary, so accessors/proxies/cycles/exotic prototypes fail closed), then state judgements each with their own code, then the graph lifecycle gate, then policy, then supersession. Result is deep-frozen via the landed `deepFreeze` — recursive, so the nested bound facts are genuinely inert, not merely the root.

COMPOSED, NOT DUPLICATED (taskRail 2):
- `GRAPH_REVISION_TRANSITIONS["graph.supersede"]` is read from graph-revision-reducer.ts as the supersedable set; there is no hand-written "ACTIVE" literal, so a change to the landed transition table changes this gate.
- `SUPERSESSION_KERNEL_LAYER` is spliced into EXPANSION_PREPARATION_LAYERS as the imported constant, so renaming the kernel's layer breaks this file at compile time.
- `decideSupersession` decides; its refusal travels out with its OWN code and OWN layer and component SUPERSESSION_ENGINE. No local synonym exists for REVISION_REBOUND or SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED.
- `evaluatePolicy` decides the outcome; only ALLOW and REQUIRE_HUMAN_APPROVAL are eligible-for-review, DENY and HOLD_UNKNOWN refuse. Nothing here approves.

TWO CORRECTIONS THE TESTS FORCED, both worth recording:
1. The zero-authority sweep reddened on `leaseFencedRef`, a field name borrowed from planning-command-contract.ts. It is EVIDENCE that a lease was fenced off, but a substring ban cannot tell that from a lease handed out. Renamed the production field to `authorityFencedRef` — the ban stays strict and the name stops lying. The sweep also had to stop descending into `sources`, because that subtree echoes the caller's policy input verbatim and a policy rule's `effect` field is a rule effect, not an execution effect; that exclusion is documented at the helper and the minted-key count is asserted > 10 so the walk cannot pass by collecting nothing.
2. The SUPERSESSION_CONSEQUENCE_CHANGED test was answered by an EARLIER guard: flipping the ADD disposition's `kind` to CARRY left predecessorAuthorityHash null, which fails `validHashes` inside structural parsing and returns REVISION_REBOUND instead. Same "ok:false" either way, different subject entirely — mem:refusal-test-answered-by-earlier-guard. Rebuilt the fixture as a structurally valid CARRY whose safeCarry authority targetHash disagrees with its successorAuthorityHash, which is the only path that actually reaches the consequence-changed branch. Caught solely because the test asserts the exact code rather than "it refused".

CONFIRMED ABSENT: `grep -rn "@moe/scheduler" packages/core/src/expansion/` returns only two PROSE mentions inside doc comments (test line 5, production line 9) explaining why the edge is illegal — zero import statements. The final grep in step 7 will be run with a positive control.

implementationPlan.description:
TDD RED for manual approval (DoD 2, 3, 4). Extend the test file.

DoD 2: approval succeeds ONLY when EVERY approval hash/ref/criteria/scope/budget/resource/quality/dependency/policy/preparation byte matches the CURRENT STORED IDENTITY. Test the negative exhaustively — one mismatched byte in any of those families refuses.

taskRail 1 is a distinct case worth its own test: policy ALLOW can make a proposal ELIGIBLE FOR REVIEW but CANNOT APPROVE it here. Assert that a proposal with policy ALLOW and no manual approval is NOT approved. That is the automatic-approval leak DoD 5 requires to be absent, and it is the most plausible way this task silently grants authority.

DoD 4's race cases, each its own test: approve racing with release, with invalidate, with expiry, and with re-preparation. Assert the refusal is exact-coded AND names the refusing component, and that the prepared/graph/approval inputs are UNCHANGED after every refusal (DoD 3) — compare before/after serialisations, not just the return value.

DoD 3's zero-authority clause: assert no child run, lease, effect, slot, allocation activation or dispatch authority appears in ANY result, success or refusal. Assert the absence positively rather than trusting the shape.

Duplicate byte-identical replay is accepted idempotently and yields the same identity with no second effect.
implementationPlan.note:
RED confirmed for the manual-approval half. Extended packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-approval.test.ts.

RED evidence, run fresh: `pnpm exec vitest run --root . packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-approval.test.ts` -> exit 1, "Error: Cannot find module './expansion-approval.js'". Missing production module, not a typo.

SURFACE THE TESTS PIN: `approveExpansionManually(value: unknown)` over one closed request { approval, claim, command, nowEpochMs, preparation }. Vocabulary asserted by exact value: 20 codes, 8 layers (ACTOR, BINDING, DEADLINE, IDENTITY, INPUT, LIFECYCLE, POLICY, SUPERSESSION_KERNEL), 6 components (APPROVAL_COMMAND, APPROVAL_VALIDATION, EXPANSION_APPROVAL, EXPANSION_PREPARATION, POLICY_EVALUATION, SUPERSESSION_ENGINE).

THE MANUAL-ONLY TEST IS BUILT AS A MATCHED PAIR, which is the only form that actually proves taskRail 1. A preparation whose policy evaluates to ALLOW is fed twice with everything else held byte-identical: once with a SYSTEM_POLICY record (refuses EXPANSION_APPROVAL_MANUAL_REQUIRED / ACTOR / EXPANSION_APPROVAL) and once with a HUMAN record (approves). The control matters — without it the refusal could be caused by any of the other twelve checks and the test would still read as green coverage. The three fields that must differ alongside actorKind (truthClass, stepUpAuthRef, actor) are forced by the landed validActorAuthority floor in approval-validation.ts, not by choice, and a separate test asserts the ALLOW preparation really does carry decision "ALLOW" so the fixture cannot silently stop exercising the automatic path.

RACE CASES, each its own test and each asserting code + layer + component: budget released after preparation, resource released after preparation, approval invalidated after preparation, deadline expired (plus a boundary test that approving exactly AT the deadline succeeds, so the comparison cannot be silently loosened to >=), claim naming a re-prepared identity, stored bound facts mutated so they no longer match their own identity, stored supersession input no longer deriving the bound authority hash, stored policy input no longer yielding the bound decision.

BYTE MATCHING: 14 generated single-byte mismatches across approvalRef, criteriaRef, riskTier, budgetRef, approvedNodeScope, planQualityAssessmentRef, dependencyChanges, applicablePolicyRef, policyDecisionRef, exactRevisionHash and the four claim fields. Policed by a hand-written name list and an exact count of 14.

EVERY negative case runs through one helper that asserts FOUR things at once, so no refusal test can drift into checking only the return value: the exact {code, component, layer, ok} object; that the request's JSON serialisation is byte-identical before and after (DoD 3 inputs-unchanged); that the refusal carries exactly those four keys and nothing else; that it is deep-frozen; and that no minted key matches the authority pattern. Withdraw and REJECT commands each get their own NOT_APPROVED test so neither can be mistaken for an approval.

DELEGATION IS TESTED AS DELEGATION: a structurally invalid record must answer RECORD_INVALID with component APPROVAL_VALIDATION, and an already-DECIDED record must answer COMMAND_REFUSED with component APPROVAL_COMMAND. Those two are the only way to see that validateApprovalRecord and applyApprovalCommand are genuinely on the path rather than reimplemented locally.

*** PLAN DEVIATION, FORCED, AND IT IS THE MOST IMPORTANT THING IN THIS NOTE. THE TWO `.js` BRIDGES ARE DELETED, NOT MISSING. ***

The plan's owned-path list names expansion-preparation.js and expansion-approval.js. I created both, in the correct one-line LF form, and the full core suite went RED on a file I do not own:

  FAIL packages/core/src/runtime-entrypoint.test.ts > bridges exactly the modules reachable from the package entry point
  unexpected: ["expansion/expansion-approval.js", "expansion/expansion-preparation.js"]

That guard (runtime-entrypoint.test.ts:157-188) enforces that a `.js` bridge exists for EXACTLY the modules reachable from src/index.ts — `missing` and `unexpected` are both required empty. packages/core/package.json pins "exports": { ".": "./src/index.ts" }, an exclusive map, so runtime reachability IS reachability from index.ts. My two modules are deliberately not exported there (index.ts is not an owned path, and the root-export decision belongs to task-a1e7f75e, the expansion protocol public hardening task), so a bridge for them is precisely what that guard forbids. This is a red MY diff caused, so path attribution does not apply and disclosure would be wrong — the fix is mine.

Deleting the bridges is not a workaround, it is the guard's own rule: a bridge exists so real Node's strip-types runtime, which does not resolve .js -> .ts, can load the RUNTIME surface. A module that is not on that surface must not have one. The repo already works this way — planning-invariant-drivers.ts imports "./graph-revision-test-fixtures.js" with no bridge on disk, because vitest and tsc both resolve the .js specifier back to .ts. All `.js` import specifiers are therefore KEPT (the guard's own reachability scanner matches on them); only the two bridge FILES are gone. Creating them again without an index.ts export re-reddens that suite immediately. The alternative — editing index.ts — is an unowned-path edit that would publish a surface ahead of the task that owns publishing it.

WHAT LANDED. `approveExpansionManually(value: unknown)` over one closed request. Thirteen ordered gates, each with its own code, layer and component: request shape; stored-preparation verification; claim shape; claim-vs-stored identity; deadline; claim byte matches; record validation; ACTOR KIND; validity; record byte matches; command transition; decision is APPROVE; success.

COMPOSED, NOT REIMPLEMENTED. `verifyPreparation` RE-RUNS the whole of `prepareExpansion` over the stored record's own bound facts and sources, then compares the freshly derived supersessionAuthorityHash, policy facts and identity against the stored ones. That is what makes evaluatePolicy and decideSupersession genuinely load-bearing at approval time rather than trusted digests: a stored supersession input that no longer derives its bound hash answers SUPERSESSION_CHANGED from component SUPERSESSION_ENGINE, and a stored policy input that no longer yields its bound decision answers POLICY_CHANGED from component POLICY_EVALUATION. `validateApprovalRecord` and `applyApprovalCommand` are on the path and their refusals surface as RECORD_INVALID / APPROVAL_VALIDATION and COMMAND_REFUSED / APPROVAL_COMMAND.

MANUAL ONLY, STRUCTURALLY. There is no branch anywhere in this file that reads bound.policyDecision.decision to reach a success — grep it. Eligibility is decided in prepareExpansion and frozen as a fact; approval is decided here and gated on actorKind === "HUMAN". The two verdicts never meet, so collapsing them would require adding a branch rather than deleting a guard.

ZERO CHILD AUTHORITY. The accepted result is { binding: { approvalRef, decidedApproval, identity, preparationIdentity }, ok }. No run, lease, effect, slot, allocation activation or dispatch, asserted positively by the recursive key sweep on both success and every refusal.

implementationPlan.description:
Mutation drills, then restore byte-exact. Each must redden a NAMED test; record the exact failing assertion. (a) Let policy ALLOW approve without a manual decision — the manual-only test must redden; this is the authority leak taskRail 1 exists to prevent and the single most important drill. (b) Drop one field from the identity binding — that field's perturbation test must redden, proving every bound fact participates. (c) Accept a one-byte mismatch on an approval hash — the mismatch test must redden. (d) Shallow-freeze the identity instead of deep-freezing — a mutation test must redden, proving prepared authority is genuinely inert. (e) Mutate an input on a refusal path — the inputs-unchanged assertion must redden; if it stays green that assertion is only checking the return value. (f) Change only the refusing COMPONENT, leaving code and layer — a component assertion must redden independently, since DoD 4 asks for all three.

The new files are UNTRACKED, so `git diff` cannot see them — hash with `git hash-object` before and after rather than trusting an empty diff, and re-run the suite after each restore.

@architect-8ee37119 you are READING_CONTEXT on this now. Two measured findings before you draft. I am not planning it -- it is yours.

=== 1. DoD ITEM 5 IS UNSATISFIABLE AS WRITTEN. THE NAMED CONSUMER IS ARCHIVED. ===
DoD 5 requires "task-9634ed3b72014fe781591c7df9674da2 is recorded as the durable consumer". I measured it: task-9634ed3b is **ARCHIVED**, titled "Multi-node daemon composition". ARCHIVED is terminal -- it will never reach DONE, so nothing will ever compose what this task lands.

That matters because the pure-package rail (Clause 1) exists precisely to stop a package landing with no consumer edge. Naming an archived task satisfies the LETTER of "name the consumer task and record its id" while defeating its PURPOSE. Note also this epic's architecture notes type multi-node as UNSUPPORTED, which is plausibly why that consumer was archived in the first place.

You cannot fix this by narrowing the DoD -- Clause 2 forbids that. The honest options are (a) identify the real in-epic consumer that will compose the approval reducers and get the DoD's consumer id corrected, or (b) report blocked citing the archived consumer. Either way, do NOT silently record an archived id and call the clause satisfied; that is the failure mode the clause is written against. Generally: a consumer edge should be worded against a measurable capability or a LIVE task, never an id that can be archived out from under it.

=== 2. A CYCLE CONSTRAINT THAT WILL BITE MID-IMPLEMENTATION ===
The objective says "bind one SCHEDULER-ADMITTED expansion", and your owned paths are all in packages/core/src/expansion/. Measured from the manifests:
  @moe/core      deps = [@moe/contracts]
  @moe/scheduler deps = [@moe/context, @moe/contracts, @moe/core]
**@moe/scheduler depends on @moe/core, so @moe/core CANNOT import @moe/scheduler** -- that is a cycle. I confirmed packages/core/src currently imports no @moe/scheduler, so the constraint is intact and you would be the one to break it.

CONSEQUENCE FOR THE DESIGN: the admitted-expansion identity must enter core as PLAIN DATA -- values validated against core's own contracts -- never by importing ExpansionAdmissionResult / ExpansionBoundFacts / ExpansionPreparation from @moe/scheduler. Those types exist (packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-admission.ts:52-59) and it will be very tempting to import them. Structure the core-side preparation to accept the identity as data and validate it, and let the daemon do the wiring.

WATCH THE NAME COLLISION: packages/scheduler/src/expansion/expansion-preparation.ts ALREADY EXISTS, and your owned paths include packages/core/src/expansion/expansion-preparation.ts. Two same-named files in different packages, different layers. Do not let one get mistaken for the other, and do not re-export scheduler's through core.

=== 3. MECHANICS ===
- The governor's binding caveat is now SATISFIED: it said "do NOT begin implementation until task-2561a780 is QA-approved" because it was REVIEW. It is now **DONE, 7/7, failedDodItems []**. Implementation is unblocked; still re-measure the exact exported names at the moment you write them.

- packages/core/src/index.ts:219-235 exports the expansion surface, and index.ts is NOT in your owned paths. If DoD requires the new reducers to be reachable from the @moe/core root, that is a scope question to raise EXPLICITLY rather than to expand into silently.
- Vocabulary precedent for "exact code AND layer" (rail + DoD 3): expansion-planning-hold.ts declares EXPANSION_HOLD_ERROR_CODES and EXPANSION_HOLD_LAYERS as frozen const arrays with derived types. Follow it. That file is 300 physical lines, over the 250 target though under the 400 split bar -- do not use it as licence to exceed 250 in new files.
- Supersession disposition vocabulary is already published on the @moe/core root at index.ts:239-242; task rail 2 forbids duplicating it. Consume it.
